messages.author: 179fcbf8a74aa3b6
messages.subject: summarise stochastic mapps - consensus tree
parts:
Hello all!
I would like to know if there is a function in BioGeoBears to summarise the results of different stochastic mapps onto a target reference topology (such as a consensus or MAP tree), rather than just having the summary tables and histograms?

Sorry if I have missed something very obvious here, but I cannot find the information along the documentation.

Thanks a lot!
Andrea

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] summarise stochastic mapps - consensus tree
parts:
Hi Andrea,

Do you mean summarizing across multiple different topologies, or summarizing multiple stochastic maps on the same topology?  The 2nd option is basically what you get with a standard ML ancestral states estimate, since the average of all of the stochastic maps will converge on the ancestral states estimate.   The former is very challenging to imagine what is even meant -- it would be coherent to count events per-time-bin across multiple trees, or something like that, but very difficult to imagine what a consensus depiction on a single summary tree would look like. 

The problem is similar to the problem with "Bayes-DIVA", "Bayes-Lagrange", etc., 

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/biogeobears/M8zw8Kidseo

...but even more complex! 

Cheers,
Nick

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: summarise stochastic mapps - consensus tree
parts:
Hi Andrea!

It is imaginable that one could calculate, from a bunch of BSMs, the average time along a branch where a particular "d" event occurred. Then you could "paint" the branch to transition at that point.  Although -- my gut feeling is that anagenetic events are usually pretty uniformly distributed in time along a branch (I haven't dug into it).

Or, conceivably, one could have some kind of graduated color scheme indicating increasing probability of the transition having occurred on a branch. I believe phytools has this for standard characters.  It is possible to convert BioGeoBEARS BSMs into phytools format (meaning I wrote a script at some point, I could find it if needed), and then I guess one could try applying phytools's paintings and summaries, but I'm not sure this would yield much that would be useful as a visualization, given that the biogeography analyses often have hundreds of states/colors, while the phytools ones are typically 2 or 3 states/colors.

Cheers!
Nick
